entries.title: Biomarkers of NRF2 signalling: Current status and future challenges

sentences: Cellular oxidant detoxification (GO:0098869) was similarly enriched, with genes including GSTM2, GSTZ1, MGST1, SRXN1, and TXNRD1, collectively indicative of NRF2 pathway activation [1][2].

Organ signature analysis revealed that the cardiac gene expression profile was most strongly enriched for signatures associated with hepatic Kupffer cells, monocytes/macrophages, and renal tubular epithelium (each 191.3-fold enriched), driven predominantly by HMOX1, consistent with the well-established role of heme oxygenase-1 as a broadly inducible stress-response gene across multiple tissue types [1][3].

HMOX1 upregulation is a well-established marker of NRF2 pathway activation and oxidative stress [1][2][3], and its induction in the heart following 1,2-DCB exposure is consistent with the xenobiotic metabolic burden imposed by this chlorinated aromatic compound.

SRXN1 and TXNRD1, both consensus genes supported by multiple publications, were upregulated and are established NRF2 target genes whose co-induction with HMOX1 strengthens the interpretation of a coordinated antioxidant response [1][2].

The co-enrichment of oxidative stress response terms, including response to oxidative stress (GO:0006979; 12 genes, FDR = 5.76e-05) and cellular oxidant detoxification (GO:0098869; 6 genes, FDR = 3.73e-03), with upregulated NRF2 target genes such as NQO1, GCLC, CAT, GPX3, SRXN1, and PRDX3, is consistent with activation of the NRF2 antioxidant signaling pathway as an adaptive response to 1,2-DCB-induced oxidative stress [1].

Among the individual dose-responsive genes, NQO1 and GCLC emerged as the most consistently supported markers of NRF2 pathway activation, with both genes identified as robust cross-tissue NRF2 biomarkers in the recent literature [1].

NQO1, GCLC, SRXN1, CYP2E1, BAX, CASP1, CAT, and ATF4 are each supported by multiple independent publications and are classified as consensus genes in the supporting literature database [18][11][1][12][4][21].

The microRNA in cancer pathway (hsa05206; FDR = 5.82 × 10⁻⁷) and the fluid shear stress and atherosclerosis pathway (hsa05418; FDR = 6.61 × 10⁻⁷) were also highly enriched, the latter defined by the KEAP1–NFE2L2–NQO1–HMOX1 axis together with PRKAA1 and SQSTM1, consistent with a canonical electrophilic/oxidative stress response [1].
Canonical NRF2 target genes—NQO1, HMOX1, GCLC, GCLM, SRXN1, and TXNRD1—were all upregulated, constituting a well-validated biomarker panel for NRF2 pathway activation [1, 2].

Confidence in the biological interpretation is high for the KEAP1–NFE2L2–NQO1–HMOX1 axis, which is supported by multiple independent high-citation publications and is represented by a coherent, directionally consistent gene set across pathway, GO, and organ signature analyses [1, 2, 22, 28].

The enrichment of NQO1, GCLC, SRXN1, and TXNRD1 among the top GO terms is consistent with activation of the NRF2 signaling axis, which coordinates the transcriptional induction of cytoprotective and antioxidant genes in response to electrophilic and oxidative insults [1].

NQO1, a two-electron reductase and established NRF2 target gene, was also upregulated and, together with GCLC, SRXN1, and TXNRD1, constitutes a well-validated panel of NRF2 activity biomarkers applicable across multiple cell types and species [1].

Confidence in the biological interpretation of the 1,2-DCB lung transcriptomic response is high for the oxidative stress, glutathione metabolism, and NRF2 pathway findings, which are supported by multiple independent consensus genes with extensive cross-study literature validation [1, 18, 31]; confidence is moderate for the ferroptosis and mitophagy-related findings, which rest on a smaller number of contributing genes, and lower for the innate immune and antiviral response signatures, which, while statistically significant, lack direct mechanistic precedent in the context of chlorinated benzene inhalation toxicology.

statements: GCLC, GCLM, HMOX1, NQO1, SRXN1 and TXNRD1 are robust markers for NRF2 activity across multiple cell types.
There is a need for consensus on the most relevant set of genes/proteins that best represent NRF2 activity in different contexts.

entries.title: An Overview of Nrf2 Signaling Pathway and Its Role in Inflammation

statements: Nrf2 plays a pivotal role in controlling antioxidant gene expression and exerting anti-inflammatory functions.
The Nrf2/antioxidant response element (ARE) system regulates inflammatory mediators, NF-κB pathway, and macrophage metabolism.
Modulation of the Nrf2-dependent pathways could be a new strategy for targeting immune responses.

entries.title: Rutaecarpine Protects against Acetaminophen-Induced Acute Liver Injury in Mice by Activating Antioxidant Enzymes

sentences: CYP2E1, also a consensus gene (14 papers), was upregulated and contributed to both the metabolic pathway enrichment and the xenobiotic stimulus GO cluster; CYP2E1 induction is recognized as a key mediator of oxidative stress through generation of reactive metabolites [4][5].

Enrichment in liver reference signatures (4.66-fold) was notable and reflected the overlap of xenobiotic metabolism and lipid oxidation gene sets between kidney and liver, consistent with the known hepatic and renal co-targeting of halogenated aromatic compounds [4][13].

CYP2E1 was upregulated and is a well-characterized mediator of oxidative bioactivation of halogenated solvents; its induction is consistent with increased generation of reactive oxygen species and electrophilic metabolites that would be expected to drive downstream NRF2 activation [4][15].

NQO1, GCLC, SRXN1, CYP2E1, BAX, CASP1, CAT, and ATF4 are each supported by multiple independent publications and are classified as consensus genes in the supporting literature database [18][11][1][12][4][21].

GCLC, the catalytic subunit of glutamate-cysteine ligase and the rate-limiting enzyme in glutathione biosynthesis, was upregulated and has been consistently identified as an NRF2-responsive gene in models of hepatic and systemic oxidative stress [18, 4, 31].

CYP2E1, a cytochrome P450 enzyme responsible for the oxidative metabolism of halogenated aromatic compounds including 1,2-DCB, was upregulated and is known to generate reactive oxygen species as a byproduct of its catalytic cycle, potentially contributing to the oxidative stress signature observed in the lung [4].

statements: Rutaecarpine protects against acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury in mice by activating antioxidant enzymes
Rutaecarpine pretreatment decreases serum ALT/AST activities and hepatic malondialdehyde content, prevents glutathione depletion, inhibits CYP2E1 expression, and reduces inflammatory cytokines

entries.title: Binankadsurin A from Kadsura coccinea Fruits Ameliorates Acetaminophen-Induced Liver Injury Through Inhibiting Oxidative Stress by Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 Pathway

sentences: CYP2E1, also a consensus gene (14 papers), was upregulated and contributed to both the metabolic pathway enrichment and the xenobiotic stimulus GO cluster; CYP2E1 induction is recognized as a key mediator of oxidative stress through generation of reactive metabolites [4][5].

statements: Binankadsurin A (BKA) reduces acetaminophen-induced acute liver damage by inhibiting oxidative stress through activation of the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway.
Pretreatment with BKA mitigates liver injury and improves CYP2E1 expression in mouse livers.
